$comment: Dispatcher configurations. Every strategy here is a weight vector over the same scoring engine — adding a strategy is a config entry, not a class. See docs/06-parameterization-and-tuning.md.

terms.measures: Estimated wait for the new passenger
Estimated in-car time for the new passenger
Added delay imposed on already-onboard passengers
Added delay imposed on already-onboard passengers, when the call diverts the car
terms.serves: Fairness to boarded, without taxing traffic the diversion never touches

terms.measures: Added delay to other already-assigned calls
Penalty rising as the car approaches capacity
Escalating penalty on the longest-waiting call
Deviation from the car's assigned zone
Hall queue length at the pickup floor

normalization.$comment: Normalize every term to a comparable scale before weighting. Without it, waitTime (0-120s) and stopCount (0-20) yield uninterpretable weights and an unsearchable space.

profiles.$comment: Conventional collective that stops for landings it passes, and prices what that costs the people already aboard. The mechanism is DECISIONS.md § D205: without eligibility.enRouteDiversion a moving car is judged from its DESTINATION, because that was the only place the kernel could stop it, so a down call on a floor between a descending car and the lobby scores two reversals — the worst directionReversal can return — and noDirectionReversal refuses the one car already heading there facing the right way, with room aboard. THE detourPenalty WEIGHT IS NOT DECORATION AND MUST NOT BE DROPPED. Diversion makes a stop the car was not going to make: it shortens somebody wait and lengthens the ride of everybody already aboard, and collective weights only waitTime, so nothing priced that. Shipped with waitTime alone the mechanism measured as a TRADE — AWT better at every quotable cell, TTD significantly WORSE at three of five and better at none — and on vertical-city it was worse on BOTH (ΔAWT +0.715 [+0.229, +1.202], ΔTTD +4.305 [+3.062, +5.548] at 4 %). The cause was measured rather than guessed: splitting vertical-city journeys by whether they transfer, single-leg ΔTTD is −0.188 and TRANSFERRING ΔTTD is +6.763, so a diversion on leg one delays arrival at the sky lobby and the passenger waits again for the shuttle, amplifying a few seconds of stop into seven of journey. detourPenalty 0.2 fixes it, and the fix is a weight rather than code (invariant 7): against shipped collective at n = 50, paired-t 95 %, verified common random numbers, this profile is better or null on BOTH metrics at every cell and worse on neither — midtown-office 1 % ΔAWT −0.936 ΔTTD −0.326, garden-apartments 10 % −0.199 / −0.346, secure-tower 2 % −0.234 / −0.141, secure-tower 4 % −0.707 / −0.739, mixed-use-high-rise 2 % −0.428 / −0.025, vertical-city 4 % −0.705 / −1.783. benchmark/enRouteDiversion.ts pins that, so removing the weight fails a test rather than quietly restoring the trade. Two more things here are load-bearing. It declares NO role: role baseline is a derivation key meaning a reference dispatcher every study holds fixed, doubleDeck.ts and mixedUseHighRise.ts build arm lists from it, and this is a variant under evaluation. And it is deliberately absent from selectionSweep.ts PRE_REGISTERED_REFERENCE_CANDIDATES, because it would be elected reference arm on merit and silently re-baseline a comparison § D151 pre-registered.
profiles.name: Conventional collective, en-route pickup

profiles.$comment: The energy proxy is stopCount plus distanceTravelled, and the cheapest joule is the one an empty car never spends: parkingStrategy stay is the whole of this profile's stage 7. A longer adaptive dwell trades a little wait for fewer stops, which is the same trade in the door machine.
profiles.name: Energy aware

profiles.$comment: Weighting starvation is only half of fairness; the other half is keeping a call movable for as long as possible, so this profile takes the latest commitment point and the largest reassignment budget of any profile here, and turns on the sole-eligible-car override so a floor served by one shaft cannot be skipped indefinitely on load.
profiles.name: Fairness first

profiles.$comment: The profile the capacity mechanisms are named for, so it declares all three: split-demand for parallel service at a heavy landing, until-commitment reassignment so a car crossing its bypass threshold hands its uncommitted calls on, and the sole-eligible-car override so the guard against a starved floor is on while it does.
profiles.name: Capacity aware

profiles.$comment: Ten weighted terms, not the eleven this profile used to carry. It weighted rideTime at 0.3 while authoring no dispatch.callType, so it ran at the up-down-buttons default, where a landing call carries no destination and rideTimeTerm.activeWhen declares the term inert. Counted through the shipped engine at seed 20260726, rideTime was non-zero on 0 of 7435 evaluations on midtown-office and 0 of 56 on garden-apartments, with cross-car spread in 0 of 2156 decisions — a weight that is decoration in every shipped configuration, which is the exact 'configurable, tested in isolation, dead in the shipped path' shape one level up from code into data. The weight is dropped rather than the callType changed: saturating normalization maps a raw 0 to 0, so removing it leaves every score bit-identical and no published number moves, whereas destination entry would have changed the profile's whole passenger model. A profile that wants rideTime must also author callType destination-entry or mobile-credential, and policies.test.ts now enforces that mechanically for every profile in this file, from each term's own activeWhen.
profiles.name: Predictive balanced

profiles.$comment: Contract-net bidding: every car prices the contract from its own estimateCost() and the group allocates from the bids. The control arm, and it is the control arm as DATA: auction.aggregation names the policy factory (dispatch/policies/registry.ts) and auction.rounds = 1 is a sealed-bid single round, which IS the centralized argmin over the same weight vector — auction.ts proves the equality against the weighted-cost policy over a deterministic sweep, so a benchmark of this profile against the same weights under central-argmin must return exactly zero. Its treatment arm is auction-multi-round, which differs in auction.rounds and auction.reserveMarginalDelayS and in NOTHING else, so a paired-t interval between the two is an interval on the aggregation rather than on whatever stage settings two unrelated profiles happened to differ in. reassignmentPolicy is until-commitment on both arms: a car that may hand a contract back must also be allowed to lose one, and a stage-5 setting that differed between the arms would be the confound.
profiles.name: Contract-net auction, sealed bid

profiles.$comment: The treatment arm of the aggregation comparison, and the only profile in this file that holds more than one bidding round. A provisional winner may take its bid back on its own reserve price — 25 s of delay to the passengers it is already committed to, which is reachable on every building in data/buildings/ where the 600 s default is not — or because winning would push it over its own hall-call bypass threshold while another bidder stays under. Both are a car REFUSING work the group's own objective says it should take, which is the one thing a central argmin cannot express and the whole of the agent-autonomy hypothesis docs/01-architecture.md asks to be benchmarked rather than assumed. Every field outside the auction section is byte-identical to the auction profile on purpose: two arms that differ in anything else measure that instead.
profiles.name: Contract-net auction, multi-round

profiles.$comment: Operational zoning — the third kind, a dispatcher strategy and not building fabric. The bank is partitioned into one contiguous band per in-service car; zoneAffinity prices a car's deviation from its band, and parkingStrategy zone-center parks each car in the middle of ITS OWN band. Both facts come from the group controller: Simulation resolves the partition once per decision through contiguousZones and hands it to stage 3 on the observation and to stage 7 on the reposition context. The partition is never stored on a car — a car that owned its zone could not be re-zoned when a neighbour goes out of service. Split-demand at ten is the up-peak half: a lobby landing above one carload is two cars, not one car twice. repositionThresholdS 2 with repositionEnergyWeight 0.1 is the deadband a zone-center hop has to clear; at the 5 s default the whole shaft is inside it and the strategy would be indistinguishable from stay.
profiles.name: Operational zoning, up-peak

profiles.$comment: The first destination dispatcher in this file. Level 0 — DISCLOSURE. Phase 6b adds destination-panel below, which is Level 1; the two are different systems (docs/09 § 1.1) and this one deliberately stays at Level 0 — no passengerAssignment, so any car that opens still takes whoever fits and both arms stay strictly comparable on all twenty-three recorded metrics. Phase 6a needed no code at all: the seam was already wired end to end — costRequestFor forwards the destination (and, under mobile-credential, the credential) into the CostRequest, estimateCost authorizes the destination against it, and Simulation #callValue supplies the head-of-queue passenger's destinationFloorId — and nothing shipped used it, because all ten other profiles run at the up-down-buttons default. Two authored fields, no class, no branch: invariant 7 read forwards. mobile-credential and NOT destination-entry, and that is a measurement rather than a preference. DECISIONS.md D30 rules that a destination kiosk authorizes; panel-stage authorization is a core change that belongs to Phase 6b, and until it lands mobile-credential is the only shipped call type that carries the credential as far as estimateCost. Measured by benchmark/accessControl.ts's H-ACCESS-1 at the interfloor-mix operating point, seed 20260726, at that study's own coverage budget of 30 replications: destination-entry without the credential leaves secure-tower with 100.0 % of journeys unserved and no quotable AWT on 30 of 30, WORSE than the conventional arm's 33.5 % — every access-zoned destination comes back destinationAccessDenied, so the call is permanently unassignable. Under mobile-credential the same building completes 30 of 30 with 0 unserved. The previous revision of this sentence read 55 % / 259 of 300 / 34 %, from a 300-replication run no shipped entry point reproduces; it is superseded twice over, by the budget the study actually declares and by T50-D1, which made a credential-less kiosk refuse the passenger rather than the whole landing call and took secure-tower's bare-kiosk arm to zero delivered. The figure is pinned in accessControl.ts PINNED_COVERAGE and re-derived by accessControl.test.ts. On a building with no accessZones the two call types are bit-identical, so the choice costs nothing and buys the three access-zoned buildings. T30 AUTHORS weights.rideTime AT 0.5, and until it did this profile disclosed a destination that nothing priced: measured through the full matrix at seed 20260728, the shipped Level-0 profile was bit-identical to eta at 8 of 8 cells, which is a configured-but-inert shipped behaviour and the shape the standing requirement exists to catch. The blocker the previous revision of this comment recorded is gone — T16 closed C26, so dispatch/policies/fixtures.test-helper.ts's call() carries a destinationFloorId and contributionScenarios() can price the one gated term in the library; policies.test.ts pins that promotion directly. 0.5 rather than the 1.0 the study headlines, and rather than the 0.3 the bracket starts at, on two criteria stated before the sweep that produced it. FIRST, a shipped default must not make a published metric significantly worse: at Midtown Office interfloor-mix, n = 150 under common random numbers, WT95 is +0.374 [−0.303, +1.051] at 0.5 and INDISTINGUISHABLE, +0.369 [−0.311, +1.049] at 0.3, +0.620 [−0.033, +1.274] at 0.7 — but +1.010 [+0.292, +1.729] WORSE at 1.0 and +1.331 [+0.623, +2.039] WORSE at 2.0. So the tail rules out 1.0 and 2.0, and 0.7 only just survives it. SECOND, a shipped default must not be observationally inert at a shipped operating point — the whole reason this weight exists. Counted at the matrix seed and budget, 0.3 is bit-identical to eta on midtown up-peak at 0 of 81 replications, whereas 0.5 differs on 5, 0.7 on 6 and 1.0 on 16; a default that changes nothing at a shipped operating point is the defect being fixed, one notch smaller. 0.5 is the smallest bracket point that clears both. What it costs is AWT +0.295 [+0.154, +0.437] against 0.3's +0.182 [+0.048, +0.317] — D27 requires saying so — and it buys TTD −1.217 [−1.531, −0.902] against −0.993 [−1.283, −0.703] and in-car time −1.512 [−1.813, −1.211] against −1.175 [−1.451, −0.900]. The one cell where the shipped profile is STILL bit-identical to eta is garden-down-peak, and that is structural rather than a weight being too small: measured, it is bit-identical at 0 of 51 replications at 0.3, at 1.0 AND at 2.0, because every down trip there ends at the lobby and the destination carries nothing the direction button did not. 1.0 and 2.0 remain study arms in benchmark/destinationDisclosure.ts and Phase 6a's −1.562 s headline is untouched: the aggressive end of an unscalarized trade is the operator's to opt into by deriving an arm, not a constant to bake into the file (CLAUDE.md § Tuning discipline). The decomposition that attributes that headline to the weight rather than the call type moved to the derived destination-eta-unpriced arm, which is bit-identical to eta on all four metrics exactly as the shipped profile used to be.
profiles.name: Destination disclosure, credential-aware

profiles.$comment: Level 1. The landing panel names a car per passenger and boarding honours it. mobile-credential rather than destination-entry only because the shipped destination profile already is (D56); either works now that the panel authorizes (packages/core/DECISIONS-T16.md § T16-D2). This was the first profile in this file to weight rideTime, and it could be because T16 closed C26: dispatch/policies/fixtures.test-helper.ts's call() now carries a destinationFloorId, so contributionScenarios() can price the one gated term in the library and 'no weight that contributes nothing' no longer fails a profile that legitimately weights it. T16 left the weight off destination-eta on the ground that destinationDisclosure.test.ts asserted the shipped Level-0 profile bit-identical to eta, which was the decomposition attributing Phase 6a's −1.562 s to the weight rather than to the call type. T30 promoted it anyway, at 0.5, because the full matrix measured what that reservation cost: a shipped profile whose whole name is DESTINATION disclosed a destination that changed no decision at 8 of 8 cells. The decomposition survived the promotion rather than being spent on it — it moved to the derived destination-eta-unpriced arm, which is the same configuration under a different id. This profile stays at 1.0: Level 1 has already committed the passenger to a named car at the landing, so the wait-versus-ride trade it makes is not the trade a Level-0 disclosure profile makes, and the two are not required to agree. The id is destination-panel and NOT destination-dispatch, which is what packages/core/DECISIONS-T16.md § T16-D7 handed back: dispatch/policies/policies.test.ts asserts that sim/simulation.ts contains no shipped profile id as a string literal (invariant 7), and simulation.ts legitimately contains the PassengerModel literal 'destination-dispatch'. A profile id that collides with a passenger-model name makes that guard unable to tell a name clash from a real branch, so the profile is renamed rather than the guard relaxed. Liveness measured at the shipped Phase 5 operating points, seed 20260726 — see packages/viz/DECISIONS-T18.md § T18-D2.
profiles.name: Destination dispatch, landing panel

patternSwitching.$comment: Per-pattern weight sets. The optimum for up-peak is not the optimum for down-peak (CLAUDE.md § Tuning discipline), and hysteresis prevents detector oscillation. This block was authored in Phase 2, schema-validated, typed on the core barrel and cross-checked for dangling names, and READ BY NOTHING until dispatch/selector.ts; editing it changed no decision, which is the configured-validated-dead defect one level up from code into data. Three things changed when it was made live, and each is a correction rather than a preference. FIRST, timeOfDay is gone from inputs. core/ has no wall clock (invariant 3) and the kernel's time is seconds since the start of the run; every shipped operating point is a 900-3600 s window from zero, so a timeOfDay derived from it is a constant near zero wearing a feature's name — a declared detector input nothing can supply is the same defect this block was. If a scenario ever carries a start-of-day, the input comes back. SECOND, idle selects energy-aware and no longer energy-saver, which was never an authored profile: config/parse.ts warned unknown-weight-set-profile and said pattern switching would 'fall back until it exists', which was harmless while nothing read the block and is not now — a selector silently missing one of its five regimes is a dispatcher that cannot express a regime its own configuration declares. The name is REPOINTED rather than the profile invented: energy-aware is the shipped profile whose entire design is the idle regime's objective (parkingStrategy stay, weights on stopCount and distanceTravelled, a longer adaptive dwell), and authoring a twelfth profile to satisfy a string would change every arm count in benchmark/arms.ts and every 'N of N' in the matrix without a measurement earning it. resolveWeightSets now THROWS on a dangling name; loader.test.ts drives the warning from a fixture instead of from a defect in shipped data. THIRD, membership is authored, because a detector whose pattern-to-signature mapping lived in code would put five pattern names in code and break invariant 7. Every ramp below is [zeroAt, oneAt] in the input's own units — passengers per second PER CAR — and a pattern's membership is the weakest of its clauses (fuzzy AND). The breakpoints are calibrated, not guessed: measured through the shipped engine at seed 20260728 over eight shipped operating points, the median rates are midtown up-peak lobby 0.0167 / inter 0 / down 0; midtown down-peak 0 / 0 / 0.0117; midtown interfloor-mix 0.0108 / 0.0025 / 0.0075; garden residential 0.0017 / 0 / 0.0017; garden down-peak 0 / 0 / 0.0050; secure up-peak 0.0111 / 0 / 0; mixed-use up-peak 0.0242 / 0 / 0; vertical-city up-peak 0.0088 / 0.0042 / 0. The rise points sit at the low end of that spread and the fall points below it, so each shipped cell reads the pattern its own name says. Rates are per car so one map is not silently a fact about one building's fleet size.
